session_note: Prior-session bills rebuilt from the docket file alone. The General Court's current data dump does not carry titles or sponsors for bills that finished in an earlier session, so most rows here show a bill number and docket only.

source.name: New Hampshire General Court bill status data dump
source.note: Pipe-delimited files published by the General Court; parsed by scripts/fetch_nh_bills.py. Column mapping documented in docs/METHODOLOGY.md and audited in data/raw/_discovery_report.md.

status_labels.vetoed: Vetoed; override pending or not taken up
status_labels.conference_failed: Conference refused, not filed, or not signed
status_labels.died_on_table: Died on table at session end

vetoes.title: Every veto and what happened to it
vetoes.why: Veto fights are the clearest record of where the governor and the legislature's majority split.

upcoming_events.title: Committee sessions already on the calendar
upcoming_events.why: Work the docket says is scheduled from today forward, mostly interim-study bills the public assumes are dead.

parked.title: Bills parked without a final vote
parked.why: Interim study, retention, re-referral and tabling end bills quietly. Who asked for the parking, and why.

effective_soon.title: Laws taking effect soon
effective_soon.why: Readers want to know what changes on the day it changes.

most_roll_calls.title: The most fought-over bills
most_roll_calls.why: Roll-call count is a proxy for how hard each side pushed.

died_in_other_chamber.title: Passed one chamber, died in the other
died_in_other_chamber.why: House-Senate friction inside one party is under-covered.
